title: Set 279

sentences.ko: 잠깐 하소연 좀 해도 돼? 회사에 무슨 일이든 공은 다 자기가 가져가는 사람이 있는데, 오늘은 내가 뽑은 수치를 거의 자기가 생각해 낸 것처럼 발표하더라. 한마디 하려다가 팀장님이 바로 옆에 앉아 계셔서 쪼잔해 보일까 봐 참았어.
sentences.text: Can I vent for a second? There's this guy at work who takes credit for everything, and today he basically presented my numbers like he came up with them. I would've said something, but our manager was sitting right there, and I didn't want to look petty.

alts.text: Okay, I gotta rant real quick. This guy at work takes credit for literally everything, and today he pretty much passed my numbers off as his own. I almost said something, but our manager was right there, and I didn't wanna look petty.

Would you mind if I vented for a moment? There is a colleague at work who takes credit for everything, and today he essentially presented my figures as though he had developed them himself. I would have said something, but our manager was sitting right there, and I did not wish to appear petty.

sentences.note: **vent** 는 속상한 걸 털어놓다, **takes credit for** 는 남의 공을 자기 것으로 가져간다는 뜻이에요. **petty** 는 별것 아닌 일로 쪼잔하게 군다는 느낌입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 카푸치노 들고 한 10분을 자리 나기만 기다리며 서 있었는데, 딱 한 자리가 나자마자 어떤 남자가 가방을 휙 던져 놓고 주문하러 가 버렸어. 그래서 결국 밖에 길가 턱에 앉아서 마셨어.
sentences.text: I stood there holding my cappuccino for like ten minutes waiting for a table, and the second one opened up, this guy just threw his bag on it and went to order. So I ended up drinking it outside on the curb.

alts.text: I'm standing there with my cappuccino for like ten minutes waiting on a table, and the second one frees up, some guy tosses his bag on it and goes to order. So I wound up drinking it outside on the curb.

I stood holding my cappuccino for approximately ten minutes while waiting for a table, and as soon as one became available, a man placed his bag on it and went to order. As a result, I ended up drinking it outside on the curb.

sentences.note: **the second** 는 ~하자마자라는 뜻으로 말에서 아주 자주 써요. **ended up** 은 원래 생각과 다르게 결국 ~하게 됐다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 그만두고 싶은 것 같은데, 말을 꺼낼 때마다 아내가 그럼 그만두고 뭐 할 거냐고 물어보고, 나는 아직 거기에 답이 없어. 그래서 그냥 이번 달만 안 좋은 거라고 스스로 달래면서 매일 꾸역꾸역 출근하고 있어.
sentences.text: I think I want to quit, but every time I bring it up, my wife asks what I'd do instead, and I don't have an answer yet. So I just keep going in every day telling myself it's just a bad month.

alts.text: I kinda wanna quit, but whenever I mention it, my wife's like, okay, then what would you do? And I've got nothing yet. So I just keep showing up every day telling myself it's just a bad month.

I think I would like to resign, but each time I raise the subject, my wife asks what I would do instead, and I do not yet have an answer. Therefore, I continue to go into work every day and tell myself that it is simply a difficult month.

sentences.note: **bring it up** 은 어떤 이야기를 꺼내다라는 뜻이에요. **keep going in** 은 계속 출근하다, 회사에 계속 나가다라는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 달리기하러 나가려고 신발까지 신고 있었는데, 그때 여동생한테서 전화가 와서 결국 한 시간이나 통화했어. 끊고 보니 밖이 벌써 깜깜해서 그냥 내일 가야겠다 싶었어.
sentences.text: I was literally putting my shoes on to go for a run, but then my sister called, and we ended up talking for an hour. By the time I hung up it was dark out, so I figured I'd just go tomorrow.

alts.text: I'm literally lacing up my shoes for a run, and then my sister calls and we end up talking for an hour. By the time I get off the phone it's dark, so I'm like, eh, tomorrow.

I was in the process of putting on my shoes to go for a run when my sister called, and we ended up speaking for an hour. By the time the call ended, it was already dark outside, so I decided I would go tomorrow instead.

sentences.note: **hung up** 은 전화를 끊었다는 뜻이에요. **I figured** 는 ~하는 게 낫겠다 싶었다처럼 스스로 판단을 내릴 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 집 계약이 3월에 끝나는데, 좀 더 넓은 데로 가고 싶긴 해. 근데 월세가 너무 올라서 방 하나 더 있는 데로 가면 한 400달러는 더 내야 할 거야. 그래서 그럴 만한 가치가 있는지, 아니면 그냥 여기 계속 살면서 짐을 좀 정리해야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: Our lease is up in March, and I kind of want a bigger place, but rent's gone up so much that we'd be paying like four hundred dollars more for one extra room. So I don't know if it's worth it, or if we should just stay and get rid of some stuff.

alts.text: Lease is up in March, and I kinda want a bigger place, but rent's gone up so much we'd be paying like four hundred bucks more for one extra room. So I dunno if it's worth it, or if we should just stay put and toss some stuff.

Our lease ends in March, and I would like a larger home, but rent has increased so much that we would be paying approximately four hundred dollars more for one additional room. I am therefore unsure whether it is worthwhile, or whether we should simply remain and dispose of some of our belongings.

sentences.note: **lease is up** 은 임대 계약 기간이 끝난다는 말이에요. **get rid of** 는 물건을 버리거나 처분하다, casual 의 **stay put** 은 옮기지 않고 그 자리에 그대로 있다는 뜻입니다.
